event.asset: DT120 (lysergide tartrate ODT, LSD) Phase 3 pivotal trial in generalized anxiety disorder: Voyage (NCT06741228), sponsored by Definium Therapeutics
event.title: DT120 Voyage GAD Phase 3 trial reports its topline primary result
event.proposition: Definium Therapeutics reports the topline primary endpoint result of the Voyage Phase 3 trial (NCT06741228) of DT120 in generalized anxiety disorder (either direction).
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first public report of the Voyage trial's primary endpoint result: Definium Therapeutics' topline press release, a results posting on the ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06741228, or the first peer-reviewed publication that reports the primary result, whichever is first. The result may be positive or negative; the event is about a primary result being reported. An enrollment-complete or last-patient-visit announcement, an interim safety update, a conference abstract without the primary endpoint estimate, or a readout of a different DT120 trial (for example the MDD trial EMERGE) does not count.

resolution_source.name: Definium Therapeutics topline press release; ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06741228 as secondary source

readings: 'Their GAD readout, which is expected later this year' is read as: Definium Therapeutics reports the topline primary result of its GAD Phase 3 program in 2026. The author names that trial in the same post as Voyage, NCT06741228 (the registry bullet coded at owen-2281), so the event is written on that trial.
The claim is about timing, so the event resolves on the first public report of the primary result in either direction, not on whether the endpoint is met.
'Later this year' = by 31 December 2026 (anchors.json: a year means its last day; origin anchor).
'Readout' = public report of topline primary-endpoint data. An announcement that the trial has completed or that data are in hand, without the result, does not count.

'Is expected' is written in the author's own voice with no source cited, so it is read as his expectation (bin B). A coder who reads it as relayed company guidance would code REPORT; that reading is logged here.

records.stage_note: Phase 3 pivotal trial Voyage (NCT06741228): per the author's registry bullet in the same post, it started 11 December 2024 with primary completion projected for July 2026, and the parallel MDD Phase 3 (EMERGE) had read out the week before the post. No class in base-rates.json covers the timing of a trial readout, so b is null.
records.note: Third-party timing call: Definium Therapeutics, not the forecaster's organizations, decides when Voyage reads out. 'Is expected' is the lexicon B phrase 'expect': bin B, asserts true. 'Later this year' anchors to 2026-12-31. Not REPORT: no source is cited, the sentence is the author's own, and the readout is more than 30 days ahead; the registry projection he relays in the same post is coded separately as owen-2281 (same precedent as owen-1683). Not KNOWN: on the statement date the GAD readout had not happened (the author says the MDD readout came first, 'much to the surprise of us all'). Not affiliated: Definium is not in the author's affiliations list; it sponsors his RAMHT events (owen-2310), which is not a role, stake, trial site or employment, so affiliated is false and the sponsorship is logged here.

Registry bullet: the author relays the ClinicalTrials.gov entry for Voyage (NCT06741228), its start date and 'primary completion projected July 2026'. The projection is the registry's and the sponsor's, passed on as information ('projected' is quoted from the record), not the author's expectation. The author's own timing call on the same readout is coded at owen-2280.

Present-tense generalization from Definium's 13-month MDD pivotal: 'it's possible to speed-run a clinical trial program', 'money is moving through the system faster', 'returns on investment are quicker'. No future state, sponsor, program, series or threshold is asserted; a description of a mechanism, not a forecast. Read as a call it would also be VAGUE (no named series for capital speed or returns).

'The actual amount of time patients are likely to sit in an office is not outlandish' is a comparative without a benchmark: no hour threshold, no clinic set, no series and no date. Nothing observable can be written for DT120 in-office time without inventing the threshold.

Conditional ('if the next program in this company's pipeline runs on the same clock') whose consequent, 'the implied cost of capital for psychedelic medicine drops', names no series, benchmark or threshold; 'every other CNS program may get benchmarked against it' is not observable, and 'financially material' has no measure. No quantity_threshold event can be written without inventing the metric and the series. 'Speed of capital follows speed of evidence' is a slogan.

'The psychedelic medicines are coming' names no drug, regulator, decision type (approval, launch, coverage) or threshold, and 'are coming' is not a deadline. 'Is it possible that this will work? I think the answer is yes' has no referent for 'this' that an event could be written on (the field, the business model, DT120). Same reading as the identical phrase in owen-1418. 'Are coming' would be bin A, but there is no event.

'Their effect sizes are going to be undeniable' has no endpoint, effect-size threshold, trial or comparator; 'undeniable' is a slogan and 'as remarkable as GLP-1s are for metabolic disorders' is a comparative without a measurable benchmark. The list of seven treatment classes is a countable set, but the outcome cannot be written as a criterion without inventing the threshold. No date.

Evaluation of a present result (EMERGE is 'great before we've even optimized workflows, business models, care pathways...'). 'When psychedelic research becomes psychedelic medicine' presupposes a transition but asserts no observable event, body, threshold or date. Descriptive praise, not a forecast.

'Bigger, better results are possible for our patients' is a comparative without a benchmark: no trial, endpoint, effect-size threshold, program or date. 'Are possible' would be bin C, but no event can be written.

The author's own words describe the pace ('this really is moving quickly') and the team ('seems like a serious team working to make sure they stick the landing on commercialization'). They assert no event: 'working to make sure they stick the landing' is an assessment of effort, not a claim that COMP360 launches. The only date, launch 'expected in first half of 2027', is in the Compass Pathways bullet he quotes, not in his words (THIRD_PARTY if extracted). A coder who reads his sentence as adopting that timeline would write a company_event on the COMP360 US commercial launch with deadline 2027-06-30 (anchor, 'first half of 2027'); that reading is logged. Comedic post format, but the comment reads sincere. The author has no affiliation with Compass.

Procedural promise by Radial (the author is its Chief Medical Officer) to email contributors whose videos are selected: the author's own organization decides both the selection and the email. Also outside the five areas. The identical boilerplate in the 13 July post is owen-2298 (a different post, so not DUPLICATE).

The negative policy call the finder reads (US firearm means-restriction policy will not change) is not in the author's words; no body, law, bill or date is named. The preceding sentence ('We should do more of this') is normative. Descriptive, not a forecast; a firearm-policy claim would also sit outside the five areas.

Restated announcement of the author's own RAMHT live event at Psych Congress on 14 September 2026 (organizer per the affiliations list). Own organization decides; a different post from owen-2279, so not DUPLICATE. Also outside the five areas.

Hypothetical consequence of an exhortation ('Let's make getting help for suicide a great customer experience. Then, everyone will want suicide prevention treatment'). 'Everyone will want' has no countable set, series or threshold; 'would make you more likely to prevent suicide for yourself' and 'might even recommend' have no measure. The antecedent is a proposal, not an observable condition. No practice_adoption or quantity_threshold event can be written.

Scheduled information, not an expectation: the two TMS CPT coding proposals (Tab 92 bundled 'omakase', Tab 53 a la carte) 'go before the AMA's CPT Editorial Panel this September' relays the AMA panel's published agenda. The author makes no call on the panel's decision. Passing on another organization's schedule fits REPORT; KNOWN is the alternative reading (the agenda is announced by the deciding body). If the author calls the outcome elsewhere, that is a separate item. He discloses Radial (accelerated TMS provider, where he is CMO), Ampa and Neurolief roles in this post.

Administrative deadline relayed from the AMA: the interested-party comment window on the TMS CPT proposals 'closes August 10' (2026), 25 days after the 16 July post, another organization's action 30 days or less ahead. Information, not an expectation; the author urges readers to comment by that date and makes no call on the panel's decision.

'Others still will use EEG to calibrate treatment' sits in a list of present-tense practice descriptions ('some practices want... others want... yet others feature fMRI') and reads as habitual. 'Others' is a quantifier with no countable set, and there is no adoption series, threshold or date. No practice_adoption event can be written without inventing the measure.

A 'may or may not' hedge, written in 2022 and reposted on 2026-07-19, on whether the report that a pizza-box video led Romanian authorities to Andrew Tate would 'prove to be actually true'. A celebrity arrest report is none of the five areas. The hedge also asserts nothing either way.

The author's own clinical practice ('one thing I haven't routinely done is measure the brain itself as part of clinical care... That may need to change'): whether he adopts qEEG in his own care is his own decision. Own-practice adoption, hedged and normative in form ('may need to'); never scored.

The author's own future use of Firefly Neuroscience's Evoke system in his clinical practice ('I haven't used it in clinical practice yet... I think it's only a matter of time'). His own decision; 'only a matter of time' is also not a deadline. Own-practice adoption, never scored. Firefly is not in his affiliations list, but the actor in the claim is the author himself.

'EEG might be one such tool' for measuring change in 'Brain Medicine' names no adopting body, guideline, device clearance, series or threshold, and has no date. 'That change needs to be measured' is normative. A hedged general adoption call with nothing observable to write.
